note: Acervo ships this list of providers, never a credential. `keyEnv` and `requires` name environment variables; a value never appears here. Row order is the default preference order: with ACERVO_TEXT_CHAIN unset, every row this deployment is credentialed for serves the kind, in this order, and a 429 from one spends a call on the next.

providers.label: Gemini (free tier)
providers.notes: 500 text requests a day at no cost; a 429 is the free tier being exhausted, not an outage. Image and audio have their own, much smaller free allowances and are usually exhausted — text is what this row is for. The `pro` speech model rather than `flash`: both are out of free quota, but `flash-preview-tts` answers with no candidates at all and LiteLLM's speech bridge raises IndexError on that instead of reporting the refusal, which would reach the chain as terminal rather than as rate limiting. Temperature is deliberately unset: LiteLLM recommends leaving Gemini 3+ at its default.

providers.label: Vertex AI
providers.notes: Application default credentials, not an API key: LiteLLM has no Vertex express-key path (BerriAI/litellm#21036). Present on a workstation that has run `gcloud auth application-default login`; on a server it needs a service-account JSON and GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS. The image model is a Gemini one rather than Imagen, which no Imagen id was reachable in this project: it is also the model the sense-image pipeline already uses. Location stays `global`; the Gemini image models 404 in a named region.

providers.label: Cloudflare Workers AI
providers.notes: Workers AI has no account-less endpoint, so the account id is required as well as the token. LiteLLM covers text only: image and audio go through the hand-written adapter, because FLUX.2 Klein needs multipart/form-data even for a text-only prompt. Audio is Deepgram Aura rather than melotts: melotts answers Spanish with AiError 8002 and answered a plain English word with a 500, which is what its own note here used to warn about. Aura takes `text` where melotts took `prompt`.

providers.label: OpenRouter
providers.notes: One key in front of many models. Whether a schema is honoured depends on the model behind it, so this row claims the weaker guarantee.

providers.label: Ollama (this machine)
providers.notes: No credential, but declared rather than assumed: the row is available only where ACERVO_OLLAMA_URL says a server is listening. A row that were always available would make `capture_unavailable` unreachable and would send every exhausted chain at a port that is usually closed. Plan 07 is where a local model runs somewhere other than this machine.
